newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - April 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - April 10.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The cabinet and the Czech National Bank are trying to find a more advantageous mix of economic policies which would better resolve external imbalances.
- According to most experts, many businesses in the Czech Republic need to lay off employees to cut down on expenses and become more competitive with foreign companies.
- Budget cuts, which the Finance Ministry requests, will definitely be higher than the original estimate of 11 billion crowns but will definitely not reach 30 billion.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The package of economic measures which the cabinet promised to present by April 16 will probably not contain an increase in import surcharges. Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said yesterday that extra surcharges are unnecessary.
- The Slovak ambassador in Prague, Ivan Mjartan was called to Bratislava yesterday by the Slovak foreign minister for consultations on current Slovak-Czech relations.

- The cabinet approved a report on the development of drug problems in the Czech Republic, which Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus presented yesterday with the statement that the condition of the Czech drug scene is critical.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Miroslav Cerbak, deputy to Health Minister Jan Strasky, is convinced that closing one fourth of the hospitals in the Czech Republic will bring about more quality health care.
- According to the general director of Cesko-Rakouska Pojistovna, Marek Venuta, the insurance company will merge with Austria-Collegialitat in a few months.
- The Swedish company AssiDoman bought Empack, a domestic manufacturer of packing materials.
- Helicopter Praha, which was unsuccessful in the tender for operating an airborne rescue service, sent an official objection to Health Minister Jan Strasky over the results of the tender.

PRAVO - On Friday afternoon, Health Minister Jan Strasky should meet with the association of large drug distributors (AVEL) to discuss the association's proposed agreement on paying off large debts owed to firms by hospitals. This meeting should end the small war which has been going on since the beginning of April.

- Transgas will sign a 20 year contract with the Norwiegan companies Statoil, Norsk Hydro and Saga Petroleum on April 14 for the supply of 53 billion cubic metres of natural gas to the Czech Republic.
